neighbours.label: the verb in reader-addressed limit or maximum constructions: 'only so many X you can <verb>', 'you must <verb> as many X as possible'
fire: There are only so many hours in a day you can spend on homework.
To pass the exam you need to memorize as many formulas as you can.
There's only so much coffee you can drink before your hands shake.
In this game you must collect as many coins as possible before time runs out.
There are only so many times you can watch the same movie.
To get better at chess you should study as many openings as possible.
There is only so much advice you can give a stubborn teenager.
Before the trip, try to learn as many local phrases as you can.
quiet: Most students spend a few hours a day on homework.
The exam covers about twenty formulas from the first term.
Too much coffee makes your hands shake in the morning.
In this game the coins disappear when time runs out.
We watched the same movie three times last winter.
Chess books usually describe the main openings in detail.
Stubborn teenagers often ignore advice from their parents.
Before the trip, the guide taught us a few local phrases.
